can you look at the changes in this branch and let me know what effort it is to fix this: 

The humanModified calculation at line 235 uses min(totalUserAdded, totalUserRemoved) to estimate modifications, but this doesn't distinguish between user modifications to agent code vs. user modifications to their own code. When a user modifies their own previously-added lines (e.g., removes 3 of their accumulated lines and adds 3 different ones), the formula at line 256 (agentLinesInCommit := max(0, totalAgentAdded-pureUserRemoved-humanModified)) incorrectly subtracts these self-modifications from the agent's line count. This causes agent contributions to be undercounted when users edit their own code between or after checkpoints.

   148→// CalculateAttributionWithAccumulated computes final attribution using accumulated prompt data.
   149→// This provides more accurate attribution than tree-only comparison because it captures
   150→// user edits that happened between checkpoints (which would otherwise be mixed into the
   151→// checkpoint snapshots).
   152→//
   153→// The calculation:
   154→// 1. Sum user edits from PromptAttributions (captured at each prompt start)
   155→// 2. Add user edits after the final checkpoint (shadow → head diff)
   156→// 3. Calculate agent lines from base → shadow
   157→// 4. Compute percentages
   158→//
   159→// Note: Binary files (detected by null bytes) are silently excluded from attribution
   160→// calculations since line-based diffing only applies to text files.
   161→func CalculateAttributionWithAccumulated(
   162→	baseTree *object.Tree,
   163→	shadowTree *object.Tree,
   164→	headTree *object.Tree,
   165→	filesTouched []string,
   166→	promptAttributions []PromptAttribution,
   167→) *checkpoint.InitialAttribution {
   168→	if len(filesTouched) == 0 {
   169→		return nil
   170→	}
   171→
   172→	// Sum accumulated user lines from prompt attributions
   173→	var accumulatedUserAdded, accumulatedUserRemoved int
   174→	for _, pa := range promptAttributions {
   175→		accumulatedUserAdded += pa.UserLinesAdded
   176→		accumulatedUserRemoved += pa.UserLinesRemoved
   177→	}
   178→
   179→	// Calculate attribution for agent-touched files
   180→	// IMPORTANT: shadowTree is a snapshot of the worktree at checkpoint time,
   181→	// which includes both agent work AND accumulated user edits (to agent-touched files).
   182→	// So base→shadow diff = (agent work + accumulated user work to these files).
   183→	var totalAgentAndUserWork int
   184→	var postCheckpointUserAdded, postCheckpointUserRemoved int
   185→
   186→	for _, filePath := range filesTouched {
   187→		baseContent := getFileContent(baseTree, filePath)
   188→		shadowContent := getFileContent(shadowTree, filePath)
   189→		headContent := getFileContent(headTree, filePath)
   190→
   191→		// Total work in shadow: base → shadow (agent + accumulated user work for this file)
   192→		_, workAdded, _ := diffLines(baseContent, shadowContent)
   193→		totalAgentAndUserWork += workAdded
   194→
   195→		// Post-checkpoint user edits: shadow → head (only post-checkpoint edits for this file)
   196→		_, postUserAdded, postUserRemoved := diffLines(shadowContent, headContent)
   197→		postCheckpointUserAdded += postUserAdded
   198→		postCheckpointUserRemoved += postUserRemoved
   199→	}
   200→
   201→	// Calculate total user edits to non-agent files (files not in filesTouched)
   202→	// These files are not in the shadow tree, so base→head captures ALL their user edits
   203→	nonAgentFiles := getAllChangedFilesBetweenTrees(baseTree, headTree)
   204→	var allUserEditsToNonAgentFiles int
   205→	for _, filePath := range nonAgentFiles {
   206→		if slices.Contains(filesTouched, filePath) {
   207→			continue // Skip agent-touched files
   208→		}
   209→
   210→		baseContent := getFileContent(baseTree, filePath)
   211→		headContent := getFileContent(headTree, filePath)
   212→		_, userAdded, _ := diffLines(baseContent, headContent)
   213→		allUserEditsToNonAgentFiles += userAdded
   214→	}
   215→
   216→	// Separate accumulated edits by file type
   217→	// accumulatedUserAdded includes edits to BOTH agent and non-agent files
   218→	// For agent work calculation, we only need to subtract edits to agent files
   219→	// Heuristic: assume accumulated edits to non-agent files = min(total edits to non-agent files, total accumulated)
   220→	accumulatedToNonAgentFiles := min(allUserEditsToNonAgentFiles, accumulatedUserAdded)
   221→	accumulatedToAgentFiles := accumulatedUserAdded - accumulatedToNonAgentFiles
   222→
   223→	// Agent work = (base→shadow for agent files) - (accumulated user edits to agent files only)
   224→	totalAgentAdded := max(0, totalAgentAndUserWork-accumulatedToAgentFiles)
   225→
   226→	// Post-checkpoint edits to non-agent files = total edits - accumulated portion (never negative)
   227→	postToNonAgentFiles := max(0, allUserEditsToNonAgentFiles-accumulatedToNonAgentFiles)
   228→
   229→	// Total user contribution = accumulated (all files) + post-checkpoint (agent files) + post-checkpoint (non-agent files)
   230→	totalUserAdded := accumulatedUserAdded + postCheckpointUserAdded + postToNonAgentFiles
   231→	totalUserRemoved := accumulatedUserRemoved + postCheckpointUserRemoved
   232→
   233→	// Estimate modified lines (user changed existing agent lines)
   234→	// Lines that were both added and removed are treated as modifications.
   235→	humanModified := min(totalUserAdded, totalUserRemoved)
   236→	pureUserAdded := totalUserAdded - humanModified
   237→	pureUserRemoved := totalUserRemoved - humanModified
   238→
   239→	// Total net additions = agent additions + pure user additions - pure user removals
   240→	// This reconstructs the base → head diff from our tracked changes.
   241→	// Note: This measures "net new lines added to the codebase" not total file size.
   242→	// pureUserRemoved represents agent lines that the user deleted, so we subtract them.
   243→	totalCommitted := totalAgentAdded + pureUserAdded - pureUserRemoved
   244→	if totalCommitted <= 0 {
   245→		// Fallback for delete-only commits or when removals exceed additions
   246→		// Note: If both are 0 (deletion-only commit where agent added nothing),
   247→		// totalCommitted will be 0 and percentage will be 0. This is expected -
   248→		// the attribution percentage is only meaningful for commits that add code.
   249→		totalCommitted = max(0, totalAgentAdded)
   250→	}
   251→
   252→	// Calculate agent lines actually in the commit (excluding removed and modified)
   253→	// Agent added lines, but user removed some and modified others.
   254→	// Modified lines are now attributed to the user, not the agent.
   255→	// Clamp to 0 to handle cases where user removed/modified more than agent added.
   256→	agentLinesInCommit := max(0, totalAgentAdded-pureUserRemoved-humanModified)
   257→
   258→	// Calculate percentage
   259→	var agentPercentage float64
   260→	if totalCommitted > 0 {
   261→		agentPercentage = float64(agentLinesInCommit) / float64(totalCommitted) * 100
   262→	}
   263→
   264→	return &checkpoint.InitialAttribution{
   265→		CalculatedAt:    time.Now(),
   266→		AgentLines:      agentLinesInCommit,
   267→		HumanAdded:      pureUserAdded,
   268→		HumanModified:   humanModified,
   269→		HumanRemoved:    pureUserRemoved,
   270→		TotalCommitted:  totalCommitted,
   271→		AgentPercentage: agentPercentage,
   272→	}
   273→}
   274→
   275→// CalculatePromptAttribution computes line-level attribution at the start of a prompt.
   276→// This captures user edits since the last checkpoint BEFORE the agent makes changes.
   277→//
   278→// Parameters:
   279→//   - baseTree: the tree at session start (the base commit)
   280→//   - lastCheckpointTree: the tree from the previous checkpoint (nil if first checkpoint)
   281→//   - worktreeFiles: map of file path → current worktree content for files that changed
   282→//   - checkpointNumber: which checkpoint we're about to create (1-indexed)
   283→//
   284→// Returns the attribution data to store in session state. For checkpoint 1 (when
   285→// lastCheckpointTree is nil), AgentLinesAdded/Removed will be 0 since there's no
   286→// previous checkpoint to measure cumulative agent work against.
   287→//
   288→// Note: Binary files (detected by null bytes) in reference trees are silently excluded
   289→// from attribution calculations since line-based diffing only applies to text files.
   290→func CalculatePromptAttribution(
   291→	baseTree *object.Tree,
   292→	lastCheckpointTree *object.Tree,
   293→	worktreeFiles map[string]string,
   294→	checkpointNumber int,
   295→) PromptAttribution {
   296→	result := PromptAttribution{
   297→		CheckpointNumber: checkpointNumber,
   298→	}
   299→
   300→	if len(worktreeFiles) == 0 {
   301→		return result
   302→	}
   303→
   304→	// Determine reference tree for user changes (last checkpoint or base)
   305→	referenceTree := lastCheckpointTree
   306→	if referenceTree == nil {
   307→		referenceTree = baseTree
   308→	}
   309→
   310→	for filePath, worktreeContent := range worktreeFiles {
   311→		referenceContent := getFileContent(referenceTree, filePath)
   312→		baseContent := getFileContent(baseTree, filePath)
   313→
   314→		// User changes: diff(reference, worktree)
   315→		// These are changes since the last checkpoint that the agent didn't make
   316→		_, userAdded, userRemoved := diffLines(referenceContent, worktreeContent)
   317→		result.UserLinesAdded += userAdded
   318→		result.UserLinesRemoved += userRemoved
   319→
   320→		// Agent lines so far: diff(base, lastCheckpoint)
   321→		// Only calculate if we have a previous checkpoint
   322→		if lastCheckpointTree != nil {
   323→			checkpointContent := getFileContent(lastCheckpointTree, filePath)
   324→			_, agentAdded, agentRemoved := diffLines(baseContent, checkpointContent)
   325→			result.AgentLinesAdded += agentAdded
   326→			result.AgentLinesRemoved += agentRemoved
   327→		}
   328→	}
   329→
   330→	return result
   331→}
   332→

content.text: Now let me look at the test file to understand the expected behaviors and edge cases:

Now I understand the bug and the codebase. Let me summarize the effort assessment.

## Bug Analysis

The issue is at `manual_commit_attribution.go:235-256`:

```go
// Line 235: Estimates user modifications as min(added, removed)
humanModified := min(totalUserAdded, totalUserRemoved)

// Line 256: Subtracts humanModified from agent's contribution
agentLinesInCommit := max(0, totalAgentAdded-pureUserRemoved-humanModified)
```

**The problem**: When a user modifies their own previously-added code (removes 3 of their lines, adds 3 different ones), `humanModified = 3` gets subtracted from `agentLinesInCommit`, even though no agent lines were touched.

## Effort Assessment

**Root cause**: The current data model only tracks aggregate line counts (`UserLinesAdded`, `UserLinesRemoved`), not which lines belong to whom. There's no line provenance tracking.

### Fix Options

| Approach | Effort | Accuracy | Description |
|----------|--------|----------|-------------|
| **Document limitation** | ~1 hour | Low | Accept the imprecision, add comments explaining the edge case |
| **Per-file heuristic** | 4-8 hours | Medium | Track user additions per file; assume user self-modifications draw from their pool first |
| **Line-level provenance** | 1-3 days | High | Store line ownership at each checkpoint; compare specific lines when calculating modifications |

### Recommended: Per-file heuristic

**Changes needed:**

1. **`PromptAttribution` struct** - Add `UserAddedPerFile map[string]int` 
2. **`CalculatePromptAttribution()`** - Populate per-file tracking
3. **`CalculateAttributionWithAccumulated()`** - When calculating `humanModified`, compare against accumulated user additions per file. Only count modifications against agent lines if they exceed what the user previously added to that file

**Logic change at line 235:**
```go
// Instead of: humanModified := min(totalUserAdded, totalUserRemoved)
// Use per-file tracking to determine how many removed lines were user's vs agent's
userSelfModified := estimateUserSelfModifications(accumulatedPerFile, postCheckpointRemovals)
humanModifiedAgent := totalUserRemoved - userSelfModified
```

This is a **medium effort fix** (4-8 hours) that would substantially improve accuracy without requiring full line-level tracking.

# ADR-001: Attribution Line Ownership Tracking

## Status

Accepted

## Date

2026-01-27

## Context

The CLI tracks agent vs human contributions for attribution purposes. When calculating attribution at commit time, we need to determine how many lines in the final commit came from the agent vs the user.

A bug was identified in `manual_commit_attribution.go` where the `humanModified` calculation at line 235 uses `min(totalUserAdded, totalUserRemoved)` to estimate modifications. This doesn't distinguish between:

1. User modifications to **agent-written** lines (should reduce agent attribution)
2. User modifications to **their own previously-added** lines (should NOT affect agent attribution)

**Example of the bug:**
1. Agent adds 10 lines
2. User adds 5 lines of their own (captured in PromptAttribution)
3. User later removes 3 of their own lines and adds 3 different ones
4. Current calculation incorrectly subtracts 3 from agent's line count

This causes agent contributions to be undercounted when users edit their own code between or after checkpoints.

## Decision Drivers

- Accuracy of attribution percentages
- Implementation complexity
- Storage overhead
- Performance at checkpoint/commit time

## Options Considered

### Option 1: Git Blame Against Checkpoints

Use git's blame infrastructure against shadow branch commits to determine line ownership.

```go
// At attribution time, blame the shadow tree against base
// Lines introduced in shadow commits = agent lines
func getLineOwnership(repo *git.Repository, baseCommit, shadowCommit plumbing.Hash, filePath string) (agentLines, userLines []int) {
    // git blame --porcelain <shadow-commit> -- <file>
    // Parse output: lines from shadow commits are agent-owned
}
```

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|------------|
| Accuracy | High |
| Complexity | High - requires shelling to git CLI (go-git blame is limited) |
| Storage | None (uses existing git data) |
| Performance | Expensive at attribution time |

### Option 2: Line Hash Tracking

Track ownership via content hashes of individual lines. At each checkpoint, record which line hashes the agent "owns".

```go
type LineOwnership struct {
    AgentLineHashes map[string]bool  // SHA256 of line content
}
```

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|------------|
| Accuracy | Low - duplicate lines cause collisions |
| Complexity | Medium |
| Storage | Small (just hashes) |
| Performance | Fast lookups |

**Fatal flaw:** Common lines like `}`, `return nil`, and blank lines have identical hashes. When a user removes a `}`, we can't determine which one (agent's or user's) was removed.

Even with reference counting (`Agent: 5, User: 2` for `}` lines), we'd need heuristics to decide attribution when lines are removed.

### Option 3: Position-Aware Diff Tracking

Track line ownership by file position, updating ranges as edits happen.

```go
type FileOwnership struct {
    AgentRanges []LineRange  // e.g., [{Start: 5, End: 15}, {Start: 20, End: 25}]
}
```

When user inserts/deletes lines, shift the ranges accordingly.

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|------------|
| Accuracy | High |
| Complexity | Very High - complex range arithmetic |
| Storage | Medium (ranges per file per checkpoint) |
| Performance | Must process every diff sequentially |

### Option 4: Per-File Pool Heuristic (Selected)

Track aggregate ownership counts per file, not individual lines. Use LIFO assumption: users modify their own recent additions before touching agent code.

```go
type FileAttribution struct {
    AgentLinesAdded int
    UserLinesAdded  int
}

// When user removes lines, assume they remove their own first
func estimateOwnership(file FileAttribution, linesRemoved int) (fromAgent, fromUser int) {
    fromUser = min(linesRemoved, file.UserLinesAdded)
    fromAgent = linesRemoved - fromUser
    return
}
```

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|------------|
| Accuracy | Medium - good for common case |
| Complexity | Low |
| Storage | Minimal (two ints per file) |
| Performance | Fast |

## Decision

**Option 4: Per-File Pool Heuristic**

### Rationale

1. **Solves the common case**: The bug scenario (user modifying their own code) is exactly what this approach handles well

2. **Sidesteps line identity problems**: We don't need to solve "which `}` was removed" - we reason at the file level

3. **Reasonable assumption**: "Users modify their own recent code before agent code" matches typical editing patterns - when someone adds code and tweaks it, they're usually tweaking what they just wrote

4. **Low implementation cost**: Changes are localized to:
   - `PromptAttribution` struct (add per-file tracking)
   - `CalculatePromptAttribution()` (populate per-file data)
   - `CalculateAttributionWithAccumulated()` (use per-file data in humanModified calculation)

5. **Extensible**: If we need more accuracy later, we can layer on additional heuristics without changing the data model significantly

### Trade-offs Accepted

- **Imprecise for adversarial cases**: If a user deliberately removes agent code while keeping their own, attribution will be slightly off
- **File-level granularity**: We can't distinguish "user modified agent lines in function A" vs "user modified agent lines in function B" within the same file

These trade-offs are acceptable because:
- Attribution is informational, not security-critical
- Adversarial manipulation is unlikely (users have no incentive to game attribution)
- Perfect accuracy would require reimplementing git-blame, which itself uses heuristics

## Implementation

### Changes Required

1. **Extend `PromptAttribution` struct** in `manual_commit_types.go`:
   ```go
   type PromptAttribution struct {
       CheckpointNumber  int
       UserLinesAdded    int
       UserLinesRemoved  int
       AgentLinesAdded   int
       AgentLinesRemoved int
       // New: per-file breakdown
       UserAddedPerFile  map[string]int
   }
   ```

2. **Update `CalculatePromptAttribution()`** to populate per-file tracking

3. **Update `CalculateAttributionWithAccumulated()`** to use per-file data:
   ```go
   // Instead of:
   humanModified := min(totalUserAdded, totalUserRemoved)

   // Use per-file tracking:
   userSelfModified := estimateUserSelfModifications(accumulatedPerFile, removalsPerFile)
   humanModifiedAgent := totalHumanModified - userSelfModified
   ```

## Consequences

### Positive

- More accurate attribution when users edit their own code
- Minimal storage overhead
- No performance impact at checkpoint time
- Simple to understand and debug

### Negative

- Still imprecise for edge cases (mixed modifications to agent and user code)
- Adds complexity to PromptAttribution serialization (map instead of just ints)

### Neutral

- Attribution percentages will change slightly for existing workflows (more accurate, but different)

## References

- Bug report: humanModified calculation doesn't distinguish user self-modifications
- Related code: `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_attribution.go`

# Attribution

## Overview

Attribution tracks how much of a commit came from the agent vs the user. When a user commits code after working with an AI agent, the CLI calculates what percentage of the changes were agent-written vs human-written.

This is captured in the `Entire-Attribution` trailer on commits:

```
feat: Add user authentication

Entire-Checkpoint: a3b2c4d5e6f7
Entire-Attribution: 73% agent (146/200 lines)
```

## The Challenge

Attribution seems simple: diff the base commit against the final commit and count who wrote what. But there's a fundamental challenge: **the agent and user interleave their work**.

A typical session looks like:

1. User writes some code
2. Agent runs, adds more code (checkpoint 1)
3. User edits the agent's code and adds their own
4. Agent runs again (checkpoint 2)
5. User makes final tweaks
6. User commits

The checkpoint snapshots capture the worktree state at each moment, but that state includes *both* agent work and user edits made since the last checkpoint. We need to untangle these contributions.

## Architecture

### Data Collection

Attribution data is collected at two points:

**1. At prompt start** (`CalculatePromptAttribution`)

Before each agent run, we capture what the user changed since the last checkpoint:
- `UserLinesAdded` / `UserLinesRemoved` - aggregate counts
- `UserAddedPerFile` - per-file breakdown of user additions

This happens *before* the agent runs, so we can cleanly separate "user edits between prompts" from "agent work during prompt".

**2. At commit time** (`CalculateAttributionWithAccumulated`)

When the user commits, we calculate final attribution by:
1. Summing accumulated user edits from all `PromptAttribution` records
2. Adding post-checkpoint user edits (shadow → head diff)
3. Calculating agent work (base → shadow minus accumulated user edits)
4. Computing the final percentage

### Key Files

- `manual_commit_attribution.go` - Core attribution calculation logic
- `manual_commit_types.go` - `PromptAttribution` struct definition
- `manual_commit_hooks.go` - Hook that triggers attribution calculation on commit

## Line Ownership Tracking

When a user modifies code, we need to know: did they modify agent lines or their own lines?

**Example problem:**
1. Agent adds 10 lines
2. User adds 5 lines of their own
3. User removes 3 lines and adds 3 different lines (a modification)

If those 3 removed lines were the user's own code, agent attribution should be unaffected. If they were agent lines, agent attribution should decrease.

### Approaches Considered

#### Git Blame Against Checkpoints

Use git's blame to trace line ownership through checkpoint commits.

```go
// Lines introduced in shadow commits = agent lines
func getLineOwnership(repo *git.Repository, baseCommit, shadowCommit plumbing.Hash, filePath string) (agentLines, userLines []int) {
    // git blame --porcelain <shadow-commit> -- <file>
}
```

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|------------|
| Accuracy | High |
| Complexity | High - requires shelling to git CLI |
| Performance | Expensive at attribution time |

#### Line Hash Tracking

Track ownership via content hashes of individual lines.

```go
type LineOwnership struct {
    AgentLineHashes map[string]bool  // SHA256 of line content
}
```

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|------------|
| Accuracy | Low |
| Complexity | Medium |
| Performance | Fast lookups |

**Fatal flaw:** Common lines like `}`, `return nil`, and blank lines have identical hashes. When a user removes a `}`, we can't determine which one (agent's or user's) was removed.

#### Position-Aware Diff Tracking

Track line ownership by file position, updating ranges as edits happen.

```go
type FileOwnership struct {
    AgentRanges []LineRange  // e.g., [{Start: 5, End: 15}]
}
```

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|------------|
| Accuracy | High |
| Complexity | Very High - complex range arithmetic |
| Performance | Must process every diff sequentially |

#### Per-File Pool Heuristic (Selected)

Track aggregate ownership counts per file. Use LIFO assumption: users modify their own recent additions before touching agent code.

```go
// PromptAttribution includes per-file tracking
type PromptAttribution struct {
    UserLinesAdded   int
    UserLinesRemoved int
    UserAddedPerFile map[string]int  // Per-file breakdown
}

// When user removes lines, assume they remove their own first
func estimateUserSelfModifications(
    accumulatedUserAddedPerFile map[string]int,
    postCheckpointUserRemovedPerFile map[string]int,
) int {
    var selfModified int
    for filePath, removed := range postCheckpointUserRemovedPerFile {
        userAddedToFile := accumulatedUserAddedPerFile[filePath]
        selfModified += min(removed, userAddedToFile)
    }
    return selfModified
}
```

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|------------|
| Accuracy | Medium - good for common case |
| Complexity | Low |
| Performance | Fast |

### Why Per-File Pools

1. **Solves the common case**: When users modify their own recent code (the typical pattern), attribution remains accurate

2. **Sidesteps line identity problems**: We don't need to solve "which `}` was removed" - we reason at the file level

3. **Reasonable assumption**: "Users modify their own recent code before agent code" matches typical editing patterns

4. **Low implementation cost**: Just adds a map to `PromptAttribution`

### Trade-offs Accepted

- **Imprecise for adversarial cases**: If a user deliberately removes agent code while keeping their own, attribution will be slightly off
- **File-level granularity**: We can't distinguish modifications within different functions of the same file

These are acceptable because:
- Attribution is informational, not security-critical
- Users have no incentive to game attribution
- Perfect accuracy would require reimplementing git-blame

## Calculation Flow

```
Session Start (base commit)
    │
    ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ User edits files                │
└─────────────────────────────────┘
    │
    ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ Prompt submitted                │
│ → CalculatePromptAttribution()  │
│ → Capture user edits per file   │
└─────────────────────────────────┘
    │
    ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ Agent runs, creates checkpoint  │
│ → Shadow branch updated         │
└─────────────────────────────────┘
    │
    ▼
    ... (repeat for multiple prompts) ...
    │
    ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ User makes final edits          │
└─────────────────────────────────┘
    │
    ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ User commits                    │
│ → CalculateAttributionWith-     │
│   Accumulated()                 │
│ → Sum all PromptAttributions    │
│ → Add post-checkpoint edits     │
│ → Estimate self-modifications   │
│ → Calculate final percentage    │
└─────────────────────────────────┘
    │
    ▼
Commit with Entire-Attribution trailer
```

## Example Calculation

**Scenario:**
- Agent adds 10 lines to `main.go`
- User adds 5 lines to `main.go` (between checkpoints)
- User modifies 3 of their own lines (removes 3, adds 3 different)

**Calculation:**
```
base → shadow: 15 lines added (10 agent + 5 user in snapshot)
accumulatedUserAdded: 5 (from PromptAttribution)
totalAgentAdded: 15 - 5 = 10

shadow → head: +3 added, -3 removed (user's modification)
postCheckpointUserAdded: 3
postCheckpointUserRemoved: 3

totalUserAdded: 5 + 3 = 8
totalUserRemoved: 3
totalHumanModified: min(8, 3) = 3

// Per-file tracking kicks in:
userSelfModified: min(3 removed from main.go, 5 user added to main.go) = 3
humanModifiedAgent: 3 - 3 = 0  // No agent lines were modified!

agentLinesInCommit: 10 - 0 = 10  // Agent attribution preserved
totalCommitted: 10 + 5 = 15
agentPercentage: 10/15 = 66.7%
```

Without per-file tracking, we would have incorrectly subtracted 3 from agent lines, giving 46.7% instead of 66.7%.

## References

- Implementation: `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_attribution.go`
